- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
355

1	---
2	name: horizon-start
3	description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
4	---
5	
6	Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
7	before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
8	(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
9	immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
10	ago, and their report was written for you.
11	
12	This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
13	the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
14	tenth of the session.
15	
16	## The four signals
17	
18	```bash

===== price-the-consumer-carrier =====
---
name: price-the-consumer-carrier
description: "A cross-project object-level rfl can be true and irrelevant; price the carrier the consuming statement binds, not the cheapest one to measure"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 9909d3dc-5f3d-4705-aaf8-d58930b5c898

---

When judging whether a theorem can be ported between sibling Lean projects, an object-level
`rfl` between the two projects' carriers is the cheapest thing to measure and therefore what
gets measured — and a clean result reads like progress even when it prices nothing.

Measured on AJC `ajc-rr` r5→r6 (2026-07-29), porting base-field invariance of the genus from
Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild. r5 verified that AJC's `Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` and
AJCR's `baseChangeBundle C K` agree by `rfl` (whole bundled object, structure morphism
included), with a negative control, and named the carrier as the live risk. Correct, and not the
obstacle. What actually blocked the port: the **cover** carrier (AJCR states it over
`AffineTwoCover`, absent from AJC entirely, which has `AffineCoverMVSquare`) and a **missing
brick** (no analogue of `quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv`; rederived from mathlib `lTensor_exact`).

**Why:** the theorem you want to instantiate does not consume the object directly — it consumes
it through a cover, a functor, or a class instance. Measuring the object says nothing about
whether the consuming statement elaborates.

**How to apply:** before reporting a port as blocked-on-X or reachable-modulo-X, name the exact
statement you intend to instantiate and list every carrier appearing in *its* binders. If the
carrier you measured is not in that list, you have not priced the port. Then check whether each
brick the proof calls actually exists on this side.

Related: [[absence-claims-need-the-whole-project]] (the absence half of the same discipline) and
[[cross-project-lean-port-checks]] (a green ported target hides collisions).

===== subsingleton-not-finrank-for-vanishing =====
---
name: subsingleton-not-finrank-for-vanishing
description: "State cohomology vanishing as Subsingleton (H¹ F), never as h¹ F = 0 — finrank reads 0 on infinite-dimensional spaces, so the finrank form is vacuously true and silently imports finiteness"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 17dacab2-7213-4998-90b2-32c4dd178a65
  modified: 2026-07-28T13:10:10.534Z
---

In these Lean algebraic-geometry projects, `Sheaf.h1 F` is `Module.finrank R (HModule F 1)`,
and `Module.finrank` returns `0` for an infinite-dimensional space. So `h1 F = 0` is
**vacuously true** exactly where vanishing is most in doubt, and any theorem concluding it
either needs a `Module.Finite` binder to mean anything or silently means nothing.

**Why:** stating vanishing as `Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule F 1)` is strictly stronger, and it
also turns out to need *less*: vanishing-propagation arguments go through surjectivity of a
cohomology map, which is not a dimension count. In AJC's
`RiemannRoch/Ledger/SectionDrop.lean` the entire H¹ peel chain (10 of 17 declarations) needed
neither `Module.Finite` binder — the unused-section-variable linter is what revealed it, not
foresight. The `finrank` spellings are the ones that require finiteness.

**How to apply:** conclude `Subsingleton (HModule F 1)` in the primary theorem and derive the
`h1 = 0` corollary separately, carrying the finiteness only there. When the linter reports an
unused instance binder on a vanishing lemma, treat it as a signal that the statement can be
strengthened, not as noise to silence with `set_option`. The same caution applies when reading
someone else's clean `#print axioms` line: a `finrank`-valued conclusion can be conditional in
a way axioms cannot see — see [[cross-project-lean-port-checks]].

For `x.F : X.Modules`, `IsZero x.F` is equivalent to `∀ V, Subsingleton Γ(x.F, V)`
(I landed the mathlib-absent converse `Scheme.Modules.isZero_of_forall_subsingleton_sections`

**Why:** AJC's `DivFamily.HasFiberDeg 0` only says `Module.finrank κ(t) Γ(F_t,⊤) = 0`
at each point t. That does NOT give `IsZero x.F`, for two independent reasons: (1) the
finrank junk-value trap — finrank=0 forces `Subsingleton` only under `FiniteDimensional`
(`Module.finrank_zero_iff_forall_zero`), needing proper-support finiteness; (2) even
`Subsingleton Γ(F_t,⊤)` (top sections of the fibre) is not all-opens vanishing — an epi
`q_t` is not surjective on global sections, so the "cyclic quotient of the unit"
shortcut is WRONG. O(−1) on P¹ has H⁰=0 and is nonzero: so the fully-general
`hz : HasFiberDeg 0 → IsZero x.F` (quantified over arbitrary π) is FALSE. The true
divzero producer must specialise π to a proper smooth relative curve, where the divisor
support is fibrewise finite (the honest gap sits in Picard/DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean's
documented support-vs-fibre carrier bridge, `isFinite_support_of_fibers`).

**How to apply:** to zero a sheaf, target `∀ V, Subsingleton Γ(M,V)` and reach for the
converse lemma. Never conclude `IsZero` from a single `finrank=0` or from top-sections
alone. Relates to [[subsingleton-not-finrank-for-vanishing]] and
[[generic-degree-intuition-fails-at-the-pinned-degree]].

13	# Projectivity of smooth proper curves
14	
15	A finite morphism to the projective line supplies finite Laurent two-chart
16	data, hence a closed immersion into a relative projective space.  The existing
17	nonconstant-map construction produces that finite morphism under exactly the
18	ambient hypotheses of the algebraic Jacobian challenge.

31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
32	
33	/-- A proper scheme admitting a finite morphism to the projective line is
34	projective over the base field. -/
35	theorem isProjective_of_hasFiniteMapToP1
36	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
37	    [IsProper C.hom] [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
38	  obtain ⟨pi, hpi⟩ := HasFiniteMapToP1.nonempty_finite_map (C := C)

40	  exact (p1LaurentChartData k).isProjective_of_finiteMap pi

43	the base field. -/
44	theorem isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral
45	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
46	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
47	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : C.hom.IsProjective := by

179	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
180	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
181	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) :=
182	  h (overSpec k A)

185	test object" and "it vanishes at every test ring" are the *same* hypothesis.
186

200	
201	`pic0Subgroup` is cut out by degree vanishing at every field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`

207	Together with the reduction above, this is what makes the reduced hypothesis *entirely*
208	ring-level: no scheme, open, or morphism of schemes occurs in it. -/
209	theorem exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom (A K : Type u) [CommRing A] [Field K]
210	    [Algebra k A] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
211	    ∃ phi : A →ₐ[k] K, t = Over.overSpecMap phi := by
212	  have hw : t.left ≫ (overSpec k A).hom = (overSpec k K).hom := Over.w t
213	  set psi : CommRingCat.of A ⟶ CommRingCat.of K := Spec.preimage t.left with hpsi
214	  have hmap : Spec.map psi = t.left := Spec.map_preimage t.left
215	  have htower : CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A) ≫ psi
216	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K) := by
217	    apply Spec.map_injective
218	    rw [Spec.map_comp, hmap]
219	    exact hw
220	  have hcom : ∀ r : k, psi.hom (algebraMap k A r) = algebraMap k K r := fun r =>
221	    congrArg (fun f => f r) (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom htower)
222	  refine ⟨{ __ := psi.hom, commutes' := hcom }, ?_⟩
223	  ext : 1
224	  exact hmap.symm

237	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (q q' : PicEtAff C A),
238	      (∀ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A),

240	      (∀ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A),

242	      q = q')
243	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
244	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
245	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
246	  refine (picEtAffineEquiv C A).injective ?_
247	  refine h A (picEtAffineEquiv C A s.1) (picEtAffineEquiv C A t.1) ?_ ?_
248	  · intro K _ _ tt
249	    rw [MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
250	    exact s.2 K tt
251	  · intro K _ _ tt
252	    rw [MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
253	    exact t.2 K tt

9	/-!
10	# A `pic⁰` CLASS OVER A TEST **RING** IS TRIVIAL ON EVERY FIBRE
11	
12	The one surviving instance of the hypothesis both live routes to a `rep` producer pass through
13	is the **ring** case of the degree-zero vanishing:
14	
15	  `∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))`
16	
17	`Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean` closed every **field** instance at genus `0`, and
18	`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the affine binder *is* the `∀ T` binder.  What
19	separates the two is a rigidity statement over a base ring, and the classical route to it —
20	cohomology and base change — consumes a **fibrewise** hypothesis.
21	
22	**This file supplies that hypothesis, as a theorem rather than a binder.**  For a `pic⁰` class
23	over an arbitrary test ring `A`, at genus `0`:
24	
25	* its restriction along every field point of `overSpec k A` is `1` (`fibre_eq_one`);
26	* its fibre Čech class at every prime `p` of `A` has `classDeg κ(p) = 0`
27	  (`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented`, via the DAT-4 seam).
28	
29	## SUPERSEDED IN PART — read this before citing the first two theorems
30	
31	A fresh-context audit of this file (accepted in full) established two things about its own
32	content, and both are recorded here rather than in a commit message nobody reads:
33	
34	1. **`Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean:104` has the same statement at an ARBITRARY
35	   test object.**  `fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup` is `pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero`

38	   landed more general lemma* and should not be cited as independent results; cite that one.
39	   The residue-field corollary is a one-line instantiation of it too.
40	2. **The lead theorem's proof does not use its own subject.**  `pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero`
41	   is `Subsingleton.elim` on the target group, so `lam`, `t` and `pic0Map` appear in the
42	   statement and contribute nothing to the proof — the probe replacing the subject by an
43	   arbitrary element of the target closes identically.  The "mechanism" the docstring below
44	   describes (`pic0Map` landing in `pic0Subgroup` through `degAt_picEtMap`) is work done by the
45	   *type ascription*, not by the proof term.  That is not a defect in the statement, which is
46	   true and is the shape consumers want; it does mean the theorem is cheap, and it was first
47	   presented here as though the mechanism were the content.

50	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented`: the DAT-4 seam application that turns the
51	membership into a *degree* equation at each prime, which is the spelling
52	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` consumes.  It is two tactic lines and it is not duplicated.

54	## What consumes this, and in which spelling

56	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine on a
57	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under exactly

59	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
60	
61	and its own `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts a *degree-`0`* hypothesis at
62	a prime into that triviality at genus `0`.  So the engine's binder is reachable from a `pic⁰`
63	membership, and this file is the reduction that reaches it: `htriv_of_pic0` composes the two.
64	
65	The residue-field instantiation is written out and is **not** a restatement of the field-point
66	form: `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps `A →ₐ[k] K` into fields, and the
67	engine quantifies over primes of `A`.  A prime's residue field is such a `K` and
68	`IsLocalRing.residue ∘ algebraMap` such a map, but the instantiation has to be written for the
69	consumer to fire — recorded because the two spellings look interchangeable and are not

74	Membership in `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)` is degree vanishing at every field point.  The

76	distance from them to the ring case carries no Riemann–Roch, no `χ`, no chart and no divisor: it

78	ring case, not a discharge of it.

81	of this paragraph asserted it of every statement in the file.

88	
89	* **It does not prove the ring case.**  Fibrewise triviality is strictly weaker than triviality
90	  over `A`: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails to synthesize even *given*
91	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)` (measured, `lake env lean`), so no chart or fibre argument

95	  (`h : picEtAffineEquiv C A lam = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C _ L)`), because the DAT-4 seam

104	  class over a test ring restricts to `1` at every field point, at genus `0`.
105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — the same at the residue

107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` — the fibre Čech class of a
108	  cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class has degree `0` at every prime.
109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.pic0_fibre_eq_one` — non-vacuity: the same at `ℙ¹` over an arbitrary

138	This consumes the degree binder completely: the conclusion mentions no degree.  It is the
139	fibrewise hypothesis of cohomology-and-base-change, available at genus `0` for *every* class at
140	*every* prime simultaneously — no locus, no openness, no spreading-out. -/
141	theorem pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
142	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
143	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
144	    pic0Map C t lam = 1 :=
145	  @Subsingleton.elim _
146	    (subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero C K hg) _ _
147	
148	/-- The same in the underlying `picEt` group: the restricted class is the trivial class. -/
149	theorem picEtMap_pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
150	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
151	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
152	    picEtMap C t (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A)) = 1 :=
153	  fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup C hg lam K t
154	
155	/-! ## The residue-field spelling: what the ring-datum engine quantifies over -/
156	
157	/-- **The fibrewise triviality at the residue field of a prime.**
158	
159	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` quantifies its `htriv` binder over `PrimeSpectrum B`, while
160	`pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps into fields.  A prime's residue field
161	`κ(p)` is a field extension of `k` (through `A`), and the field point of `overSpec k A` at `p` is
162	`Over.overSpecMap` of the composite algebra map — so the two quantifiers match, but only once
163	this instantiation is written.
164	
165	Recorded as its own declaration for exactly that reason: "residue fields are field points" is
166	true and is not a proof that a consumer indexed by primes can fire. -/
167	theorem pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
168	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
169	    (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
170	    pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap
171	        ((Algebra.ofId A p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)) lam = 1 :=
172	  pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero C hg lam _ _
173	
174	/-! ## The degree of the fibre Čech class -/
175	
176	/-- **The fibre Čech class of a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class has degree zero**, at every
177	`k`-algebra map into a field — in particular at every residue field.
178	
179	Route: the DAT-4 seam `degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk` (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`)
180	identifies `degAt lam (Over.overSpecMap φ)` with `classDeg K` of the pulled-back Čech class, and
181	membership in `pic0Subgroup` says the left side is `0`.
182	
183	This is the form a consumer holding a *degree* hypothesis at a prime wants: the ring-datum
184	engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts it to triviality of the fibre
185	class at genus `0`. -/
186	theorem classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented
187	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
188	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left.CechPic)
189	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C A (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A))
190	      = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) L))
191	    (φ : A →ₐ[k] K) :
192	    classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) = 0 := by
193	  rw [← degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk φ (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A)) L h]
194	  exact lam.2 K (Over.overSpecMap φ)
195	
196	/-! ## Non-vacuity: the statements fire at a curve, unconditionally -/
197	
198	/-- **Fibrewise triviality at `ℙ¹`, with no hypothesis.**
199	
200	`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` supplies `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` over an arbitrary field and
201	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` the three curve binders, so the theorem above applies with nothing left to
202	discharge.  Recorded because a fibrewise hypothesis nobody can instantiate is worth nothing, and
203	this one is instantiated at a real curve over an arbitrary field. -/
204	theorem P1.pic0_fibre_eq_one (k : Type u) [Field k]
205	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
206	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k A))
207	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
208	    pic0Map (P1.asOver k) t lam = 1 :=
209	  pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k) lam K t
210	
211	/-- Non-vacuity of the residue-field spelling at `ℙ¹`. -/
212	theorem P1.pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one (k : Type u) [Field k]
213	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
214	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k A)) (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
215	    pic0Map (P1.asOver k) (Over.overSpecMap
216	        ((Algebra.ofId A p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)) lam = 1 :=
217	  pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k) lam p
218	
219	end

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0VanishingAffineReduction
8	
9	/-!
10	# AT GENUS `0` THE `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP CONDITION IS FIBREWISE TRIVIALITY
11	
12	`hvan : ∀ T, Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T)` is the hypothesis both live routes to a producer
13	of `(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy` pass through, and it had no instance.  Its field
14	instances were closed at genus `0`, and the surviving ring instances were priced as
15	"cohomology and base change".
16	
17	At `genus C = 0` the hypothesis — at *every* test object, not merely affine ones — is
18	*equivalent* to
19	
20	  **`hrig`: a `picEt` class that restricts to `1` at every field point of `T` is `1`.**
21	
22	The equivalence is `pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity` below, proved in both directions.
23	
24	## WHAT THIS IS, STATED HONESTLY — the original framing was wrong
25	
26	**An earlier version of this header called the equivalence a *repricing* and said "the degree
27	condition is provably idle at genus `0`".  A fresh-context audit (`I-1650`, `I-1653`) refuted
28	that, and the refutation is worth more than the claim was.**
29	
30	At genus `0`, for every `T` and every `lam`, the antecedent of `hrig` and membership in
31	`pic0Subgroup C T` are *equivalent* — forward by `degAt_one` after rewriting the restriction to
32	`1`, backward by `fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup` below.  So `hrig` is `hvan` **with the same
33	predicate written differently**: `= 1` in place of `deg = 0`.  The degree left the notation, not
34	the mathematics.  The tell was visible in this file all along — `rigidity_of_pic0Vanishing`
35	needs *no genus hypothesis*, and a genuinely weaker target does not round-trip for free.
36	
37	**What the new spelling does buy, and it is not nothing.**  `classDeg` carries five instance
38	binders on the fibre curve (`IsIntegral`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `QuasiCompact`, and
39	both `Module.Finite` Betti-number clauses) which do not synthesize through the `relCurve` `def`
40	barrier — all five measured as genuinely required.  The triviality spelling needs none of them,
41	so hypotheses that could not be *stated* at a general prime become statable.  That is a
42	**statability** gain, not a reduction of the obligation.
43	
44	`fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup` is the direction that is reusable on its own: a degree-zero
45	class at genus `0` is fibrewise trivial at every field point of **any** test object, with no
46	affineness.  It is what pic-g's ring-level engine work consumes.
47	
48	## The converse, and why it is worth stating
49	
50	`hrig` is not merely sufficient.  `rigidity_of_pic0Vanishing` derives it *from* the vanishing,
51	because a class trivial at every field point has `degAt` equal to `0` there
52	(`degAt_one` after transporting along the restriction), hence lies in `pic0Subgroup`, hence is
53	`1` when that group is trivial.  So the two are the same hypothesis and no strength is lost by
54	attacking `hrig` instead — the bundled equivalence is `pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity`.
55	
56	## What this does NOT do
57	
58	* **It does not prove `hrig`, at any curve**, and — per the correction above — `hrig` is not a
59	  *smaller* obligation than `hvan`, only a differently spelled one.  `ℙ¹` gains no instance
60	  from this file.
61	* **It does not make `hrig` cheap.**  Field-point separation of `picEt` has no producer in the
62	  tree either — `PicEtAff.unit_injective` and `relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover` are
63	  separation along *étale covers*, which is a different family of test maps, and a field point
64	  is not an étale cover of `A` unless `A` is already a field.
65	* **It says nothing at positive genus**, where the forward direction fails at its only step:
66	  the field-test vanishing it consumes is false there.
67	
68	## Main declarations
69	
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup` — **the reusable half**: at genus `0`, a
71	  degree-zero class restricts to `1` at every field point of any test object.
72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity` — **the reduction**: field-point
73	  rigidity of `picEt` gives the vanishing at every test.
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.rigidity_of_pic0Vanishing` — the converse.
75	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity` — the equivalence: the two spellings of the
76	  hypothesis are one hypothesis.
77	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity` — the reduction at `ℙ¹`, with the
78	  genus hypothesis discharged, so the statement has a witness curve.
79	-/
80	
81	set_option autoImplicit false
82	
83	universe u
84	
85	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
86	
87	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
88	
89	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
90	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
91	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
92	
93	noncomputable section
94	
95	/-! ## The forward step: the degree condition is spent here, and only here -/
96	
97	/-- **A DEGREE-ZERO CLASS IS FIBREWISE TRIVIAL AT GENUS `0`**, at every field point of every
98	test object.
99	
100	This is the one step that consumes the degree condition.  `pic0Map C t` restricts a
101	degree-zero class to a *degree-zero* class of the field test — that stability is definitional
102	through `degAt_picEtMap` — and at a field test the group is a `Subsingleton` by the landed
103	`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero`, so the restriction is `1` by
104	`Subsingleton.elim`.  Nothing else in this file mentions a degree.
105	
106	No affineness on `T`: the test object is arbitrary. -/
107	theorem fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup (hg : genus C = 0) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
108	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
109	    picEtMap C t (lam : picEt C T) = 1 := by
110	  haveI : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) :=
111	    subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero C K hg
112	  have h1 : pic0Map C t lam = 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
113	  have h2 := congrArg
114	    (fun z : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K) => (z : picEt C (overSpec k K))) h1
115	  simpa [pic0Map_coe] using h2
116	
117	/-! ## The reduction, and its converse -/
118	
119	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: at genus `0`, field-point rigidity of `picEt` gives the `pic⁰` vanishing
120	at **every** test object.
121	
122	`hrig`'s statement carries no degree, no χ, no divisor and no chart — it is separation of the
123	presheaf `picEt C ·` against field points.  The proof is `fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup` fed
124	to `hrig`, twice.  (Per `I-1650`: the *hypothesis* is nonetheless the same one, so this is a
125	change of spelling with a statability payoff, not a discount.) -/
126	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity (hg : genus C = 0)
127	    (hrig : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T),
128	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
129	        picEtMap C t lam = 1) → lam = 1)
130	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T) := by
131	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
132	  have key : ∀ w : pic0Subgroup C T, (w : picEt C T) = 1 := fun w =>
133	    hrig T _ fun K _ _ tp => fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup C hg w K tp
134	  rw [key s, key t]
135	
136	/-- **THE CONVERSE**: the vanishing gives field-point rigidity.
137	
138	A class trivial at every field point has `degAt` equal to `0` at every field point — rewrite
139	the restriction to `1` and apply `degAt_one` — so it lies in `pic0Subgroup C T`, which the
140	hypothesis makes trivial.  Note this direction needs **no** genus hypothesis. -/
141	theorem rigidity_of_pic0Vanishing
142	    (hvan : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
143	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
144	    (h : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
145	      picEtMap C t lam = 1) : lam = 1 := by
146	  haveI := hvan T
147	  have hmem : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T := by
148	    intro K _ _ t
149	    rw [degAt, h K t, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
150	  have : (⟨lam, hmem⟩ : pic0Subgroup C T) = 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
151	  exact congrArg (fun z : pic0Subgroup C T => (z : picEt C T)) this
152	
153	/-- **THE EQUIVALENCE**: at genus `0` the vanishing at every test is exactly field-point
154	rigidity of `picEt`.
155	
156	Read it as what it is: the *same* hypothesis in two spellings, not a smaller one.  A lane may
157	take the rigidity form without weakening anything — and the reason to do so is mechanical, that
158	`classDeg`'s five fibre instances drop out of the statement, not that the obligation shrinks
159	(`I-1650`). -/
160	theorem pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity (hg : genus C = 0) :
161	    (∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
162	      ↔ ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T),
163	          (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
164	            picEtMap C t lam = 1) → lam = 1 :=
165	  ⟨rigidity_of_pic0Vanishing C, subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity C hg⟩
166	
167	/-! ## Non-vacuity: the reduction fires at a curve -/
168	
169	/-- **The reduction at `ℙ¹`, with the genus hypothesis discharged.**
170	
171	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` gives `P1.asOver k` the curve binders over an arbitrary field and
172	`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` gives `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0`, so at `ℙ¹` the *only* thing between
173	this project and a `JacobianData` through `jacobianData_of_subsingleton` is field-point rigidity
174	of `picEt (P1.asOver k) ·`.  Recorded because a conditional statement whose antecedent has no
175	witness curve is worth nothing, and this one has one. -/
176	theorem P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity (k' : Type u) [Field k']
177	    (hrig : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k'))) (lam : picEt (P1.asOver k') T),
178	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k' K] (t : overSpec k' K ⟶ T),
179	        picEtMap (P1.asOver k') t lam = 1) → lam = 1)
180	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k'))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k') T) :=
181	  AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity (C := P1.asOver k')
182	    (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k') hrig T
183	
184	end
185	
186	end AlgebraicGeometry

20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
21	anywhere in the statement.
22

24	
25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
26	
27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
43	
44	## What this buys, stated exactly
45	
46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
51	this tree.
52	
53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
60

64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*

67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.

77	
78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
